main_text.p: ratius, Atqui vultus erat, pulchra & praclara minantis ; alibíque: unde & Gallicum mine pro vultu & exteriore fpecie:) Hector minatur, (id eft, ipsâ praefidentis oris fpecie promittit) fe aliquid locuturum. In aliis locis Homericis ubi idem verbum occurrit, non eadem difficultas, quòd manifeftior in illis jactantiae & confidentiae indicatio: ut cum de eodem Hectore ait,
Σλεῦ͂ ϛ γὰρ ὑπνῶν ἀπονώϊ̈ν ἀχρα κόρυμβα
Et Ια.β᾽. Σλεῦτο γὰρ δ᾽ χόμψῳ νικησῖμψ, εἴ ῳ ἂν ἀνλαί
Et Ιλ.φ᾽. Σλεῦτο δ᾽ οὐ ἀμφολίρων ἀπονα- λίψ ῥα χαλκῷ.
In his & similibus, de apertâ jactatione, & infolentiore gloriatione verbum ufurpatur. Hinc Angli finxerunt suum stout, quo hominem audacem & praesidentem indicant.
Σβόμβῳ, turbo, trochus: Etiam ἀνεσφῇ ἀνέμων, vertex, turbo, procella, (aliter, ῥεβίλῳ) a Cozme.

page.notes: Greek text reproduced as legible; several Greek words are doubtful and may contain errors. The handwritten marks at the top right are not printed and were omitted. The "stout" word in black letter is rendered as bold/black-letter in the margin of the English word.
